newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico to float mortgage-backed securities in '98.
newsitem.headline: Mexico to float mortgage-backed securities in '98.

text.p: Mexico is planning to issue mortgage-backed securities for the first time on the local stock exchange next year, Deputy Finance Minister Martin Werner said on Wednesday.

"We're working...with investment banks who will help us with this first issue of mortgages in the market next year, Werner told a meeting of Mexican finance executives. "It should help us generate an appetite for this type of paper."
He said contacts had been made with mortgage-backed experts in the United States, and called the planned first issue a pilot project.

Mexican banks have been saddled with spiralling mortgage defaults since December 1994, when the government devalued the peso and plunged the country into its worst economic crisis in 50 years. Securitization of mortgages would be a way of offloading some of the burden.
Werner said loans for public housing may also be included in the scheme.
